cluster_label: ovary_choriogenic main body follicle cell and corpus luteum
working_definition: A group of adult ovary cells the authors call choriogenic main body follicle cells and corpus luteum (follicle-cell-derived remnants after ovulation) (Li et al. 2022, Fly Cell Atlas). Authors gave 'Manual Annotation' (no FBbt id).
searches_performed: choriogenic main body follicle cell and corpus luteum

best_match.fbbt_definition: Follicle cell that overlies the oocyte (Wu et al., 2008). Along with the posterior terminal follicle cells they form a columnar epithelium from stage 10, which deposits eggshell components (Wu et al., 2008). These cells are connected to one another by ring canals (Airoldi et al., 2011).

additional_matches.fbbt_definition: Cell of the corpus luteum. These develop from follicle cells that are shed when the egg leaves the ovary, gaining a yellow pigmentation and upregulating ecdysone biosynthetic enzymes (Deady et al., 2015).

justification: Two named classes, each with an FBbt cell term. They share no informative common ancestor (main body follicle cell is a follicle cell / somatic cell of ovariole; corpus luteum cell is only a somatic cell), so both are given: main body follicle cell as primary and corpus luteum cell additional. 'Choriogenic' and the stage restriction are not captured by FBbt. If a single common-parent mapping is preferred, the only true common ancestor is the generic somatic cell (FBbt:00100318).

other_candidates.reason_rejected: Only true common ancestor of both members, but uninformatively generic.

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: Structure formed from the follicle cell layer of the egg chamber after the egg has been released from the ovary (Deady et al., 2015).
other_candidates.reason_rejected: Multicellular structure, not a cell term.

recommendation: Map to main body follicle cell (FBbt:00005402) broad, with corpus luteum cell (FBbt:00048551) as additional match.
